status: WIP: read-only repeated-baseline control complete; isolated PING benefit does not establish a generic mixed-workload speedup.
change: Longer repetitions of the existing fixed-command diagnostic; no production server changes, fixture access, persistent writes, or TLS policy changes.

validation.coverage: Only PING and SELECT 1, explicit plaintext/TLS verified on the client socket. SELECT 1 must return exactly ((1,),). Each command finishes before the next; connection setup/warmup are outside timing. Python/client overhead remains in timings.
validation.tls_identity: Local self-signed endpoints: encrypted mode checks TLS socket use but disables certificate identity verification. Independent Rust TLS coverage is recorded in frame-write-baseline.json.

interpretation: Plaintext PING improves against both baseline observations in all four rounds; +8.29% median versus +0.66% for the unchanged baseline repetition.

TLS PING has +2.73% median, three positive pairs versus the first baseline and four positive pairs versus the repeated baseline. The one negative first-baseline pair accompanies an even slower unchanged-baseline repetition.

Plaintext SELECT 1 is -1.22% median with mixed paired signs. TLS SELECT 1 is -0.74% median and slower than both baseline observations in all four rounds. The latter is not erased by positive PING results.

Source inspection shows SELECT 1 uses PacketIoWriter::write_packets, whose uncompressed implementation and ClientStream scalar write are unchanged by frame coalescing. Therefore these observations do not isolate a vectored-write cause for the SELECT difference; binary/server/process and time variation remain possible, unproven factors.
The longer diagnostic supports a benefit on single OK frames, not generic sysbench/TPC-C throughput. Prior all-negative TPC-C evidence remains authoritative for those runs.
